title: DIED after 90 days with hot motor and burned odor!!
text:
DIED after 90 days with hot motor and burned odor!!. ******Updated Review September 2018 Reduced to 1 Star!****

After barely 90 days of use, this fan has completely died. I have not abused it in any way at all, but today the motor got hot after running for 35 minutes on level 1 and emitted a smokey odor and stopped working entirely. I've used it almost every day for a few hours a day usually on level two, but never running 24 hours at a time and never on the highest setting. I've kept the fan clean and with plenty of air flow. It's disappointing and concerning simply because the heat and odor means something inside was trying to burn up and that could be a safety issue if it happens when you're not home!

~~~~~~Original review is below. ~~~~~
This is Texas and it's hot. Of course we have central air conditioning, but we also have multiple fans in the house and ceiling fans going 24/7 from April to November. We keep the ac at 76 degrees and the fans move the air enough that it actually feels cooler, so they are a must around here.

This one is about as basic as a fan can be without being a straight box fan. You have to assemble it - that took 8 minutes from start to finish and no tools needed. It has a nice wide turn radius for the oscillating setting and there's no rattling as it moves.

In a small room or down a straight hall, this fan puts out decent air flow that is easily felt on the medium power setting. However, in a big open room, you need to put it on full power to feel any difference more than five feet away from the fan. And at full speed, you can definitely hear that motor going. So for us, it will be a guest bedroom fan only.
